item.title: [7] Zeeman Quantum Geometry of the Layer Pseudo-spin
item.description:
Last authors: Bingxuan Jiang, Shihao Zhang

Score 7/10 B_IMPORTANT_CONDMAT

Why: Theory of Berry curvature and quantum geometry in twisted bilayers (MoTe2); aligns with moire/topological interests.

Tags: #theory #twisted-bilayer #Berry-curvature

Abstract: Two-dimensional layers coupled by position-dependent interlayer tunnelling host a layer pseudo-spin whose polarization is a controllable internal degree of freedom. We introduce the quantum geometry of this layer pseudo-spin: a mixed tensor formed from the interband Berry connection and the layer matrix element, which governs the response to an oscillating in-plane electric field. Because the layer pseudo-spin is an Ising-type scalar invariant under threefold rotation, its selection rules differ from those of a pseudovector spin. In a minimal two-band model, the layer-pseudo-spin quantum metric and Zeeman--Berry curvature are nonzero, while their zone integrals vanish. An in-plane drive therefore leaves the spatially averaged polarization unchanged at linear order but imprints a moir\'{e}-periodic intracell pattern, directly imageable by layer-resolved tunnelling. For twisted MoTe$_2$ bilayer, we quantify the local dipole modulation and identify the rectified, helicity-odd, and third-harmonic channels through which a net response appears at higher order.

item.title: [9] Spectral signatures of hidden order and hidden quantum critical points
item.description:
Last authors: Annabelle Bohrdt, Fabian Grusdt

Authors: Reja H. Wilke, Henning Schl\"omer, Sebastian Paeckel, Annabelle Bohrdt, Fabian Grusdt

Score 9/10 B_IMPORTANT_CONDMAT

Why: Direct theory support for spectroscopy (RIXS, neutrons) on hidden order and topological phases.

Tags: #theory #RIXS #topological

Abstract: Hidden-order phases elude the conventional Ginzburg-Landau framework: although they spontaneously break symmetry, their order remains invisible to standard local two-point correlators. Instead, they are typically characterized by nonlocal (string) order parameters and are believed to underlie a range of exotic quantum states, such as symmetry-protected topological (SPT) phases. While hidden correlations have previously been detected through nonlocal observables in quantum gas microscope experiments, in realistic solid-state systems multipoint observables are typically inaccessible and the signatures of hidden order remain largely unexplored. In this work, we show that hidden order in doped spin chains can be directly probed through dynamical two-point response functions measurable by resonant inelastic X-ray scattering (RIXS) and neutron scattering. Focusing on a minimal model, we numerically identify clear spectral fingerprints of both the hidden-order phase, its associated hidden quantum critical point as well as a specific group of gapless SPT phases. Complementing our numerical results with analytical insights, we uncover the microscopic origin of these spectral signatures and demonstrate how they emerge from the interplay between spin and charge degrees of freedom. Together, our results establish spectroscopy as a practical probe of hidden order and gapless SPT phases and provide a unified understanding of the low-energy physics governing these unconventional quantum phases.

item.title: [10] Stacking-Induced Tuning of a Flat-Band Surface State in NbIrTe4
item.description:
Last authors: Lukas Muechler, Sarah A. Burke

Authors: Jiabin Yu, Mohamed Oudah, Giang Nguyen, et al.

Score 10/10 A_MUST_READ

Why: author whitelist: Andrea Damascelli

Tags: #ARPES #angle-resolvedphotoemission #photoemission #STM #Weyl #quantumspinHall #quasi-1D #monolayer

Abstract: Ternary layered transition metal dichalcogenides (TMDCs) offer high tunability and access to correlated and topological states. However, like the broader family of layered TMDCs, their properties are sensitive to stacking order and interlayer coupling. Here, we investigate the electronic structure and surface states of NbIrTe$_4$, a candidate Weyl semimetal in bulk, and predicted to be a quantum spin Hall insulator in monolayer form. Using scanning tunnelling microscopy (STM), angle-resolved photoemission spectroscopy (ARPES), and density-functional theory (DFT), we attribute the strong resonance in tunnelling spectroscopy located approximately 8 meV below the Fermi level to a surface-derived flat band which shows sensitivity to the local stacking order at the surface. In regions where the top layer is laterally shifted, tunnelling spectroscopy instead shows a gap-like feature with intensity near the Fermi level shifted in energy. Combining DFT and quasiparticle interference (QPI) measurements, we find this dramatic change in the spectroscopy in the vicinity of the quasi-1D flat-band surface state becomes dispersive due to a change in the spatial distribution of the density of states in the top two layers. These findings establish NbIrTe$_4$ as a platform where surface band dispersion can be effectively tuned through local structural manipulation.

item.title: [8] Quantum Oscillations across Hole Crystallization in Rhombohedral Graphene
item.description:
Last authors: Daniele Guerci, Enrico Rossi

Score 8/10 B_IMPORTANT_CONDMAT

Why: Connects quantum oscillations to Fermi surface topology and superconductivity in rhombohedral graphene.

Tags: #graphene #quantum-oscillations #Fermi-surface

Abstract: Recent quantum-oscillation measurements in rhombohedral graphene reveal an abrupt increase in the dominant frequency and the emergence of additional frequencies as the carrier density is lowered toward superconductivity. Noninteracting band models can account for multiple frequencies but do not explain the upward jump. We show that these features can arise from two competing fates of the inner hole pocket in an annular Fermi sea: collapse into a simply connected Fermi liquid or crystallization into an anticrystal, in which localized holes coexist with itinerant electrons. Pocket collapse contracts the outer Fermi contour at fixed density, whereas hole crystallization preserves a larger contour that supports magnetic-breakdown orbits. This contrast provides a possible explanation for the frequency jump, while additional reconstructed orbits produce a multitone spectrum. Our results support the anticrystal as a candidate normal state near superconductivity in rhombohedral graphene.

item.title: [8] Ballistic transport and crystallographic control in altermagnetic quantum rings
item.description:
Last authors: Edilberto O. Silva

Score 8/10 B_IMPORTANT_CONDMAT

Why: Investigation of transport signatures in altermagnetic systems, a high-interest topic for the user.

Tags: #altermagnetism #transport #topological

Abstract: We study coherent two-terminal transport through a finite-width $d$-wave altermagnetic quantum ring with nonmagnetic leads. A confined Aharonov--Bohm flux remains exactly $h/e$ periodic and, in the symmetric one-mode geometry, produces an exact half-flux transmission zero. A perpendicular field shifts the interference pattern according to an effective area $A_{\rm eff}=1.0342\,\pi r_0^2$ and the altermagnetic splitting resolves the common zero into nearby spin-dependent nodes. Rotating the crystal reverses the transmitted spin, whereas the mirror orientation $\theta_A=\pi/4$ is exactly spin degenerate. For a $50$~nm reference ring, sub-tesla fields yield windows with $|P_T|>0.99$, the most accessible of which requires a uniform field alone and no confined flux. Finite-bias, thermal, disorder, Zeeman, and spin-conserving voltage-probe calculations show that the polarization is appreciably more stable than individual coherent-resonance amplitudes. These results identify interference-node positions, flux periodicity, and crystal-controlled spin polarization as experimentally useful signatures of an altermagnetic mesoscopic interferometer.

item.title: [10] Chiral magnetic excitations in the RMn6Sn6 kagome metals (R=Tb, Ho, Er, and Y)
item.description:
Last authors: B. G. Ueland (Ames National Laboratory), R. J. McQueeney (Ames National Laboratory

Authors: Christopher J. Ranlett (Ames National Laboratory, Iowa State University Department of Physics, Astronomy), et al.

Score 10/10 B_IMPORTANT_CONDMAT

Why: Direct hit on kagome metals and magnetic excitations via neutron scattering; highly relevant to user's projects.; demoted from A: broad CM, not direct user/project hit

Tags: #material #kagome #neutron-scattering

Abstract: Recent inelastic neutron scattering (INS) investigations of the kagome metal TbMn6Sn6 reveal novel chiral magnetic excitations associated with the kagome layer. These excitations appear to have an itinerant character with a large energy scale (> 100 meV) and heavy damping; however, the origin of these excitations, which are not predicted by local moment linear spin-wave theory, is not understood. Here, we use INS to show that chiral excitations are also found in RMn6Sn6 compounds with R=Tb, Ho, Er, and Y having uniaxial, tilted, planar ferrimagnet, and planar double-spiral magnetic structures, respectively. Thus, the chiral excitations exist regardless of the magnetic structure. Additionally, R=Er and Y demonstrate that the chiral mode intensity is weaker in planar magnetic structures, suggesting that excitations are transverse to the local Mn moment direction. The chiral excitations appear only at L=odd positions in the Brilloun zone, and correspond to chiral spin exciations of the same handedness within each kagome layer, and pi out-of-phase between layers.

item.title: [7] Magnetic-Field-Induced Darkening of Bright Excitons in a MoWSe2 Monolayer Alloy
item.description:
Last authors: Antonio Polimeni, Maciej R. Molas

Authors: Katarzyna Olkowska-Pucko, Artur O. Slobodeniuk, Mehdi Arfaoui, et al.

Score 7/10 B_IMPORTANT_CONDMAT

Why: Relevant experimental study on magneto-optical effects in a 2D material system.

Tags: #material #magneto-optical #2D

Abstract: Magnetic fields are widely used to brighten spin-forbidden dark excitons, but the inverse effect on an optically bright exciton has remained largely unexplored. We demonstrate the complementary phenomenon of magnetic-field-induced darkening of a bright exciton in Mo$_{0.68}$W$_{0.32}$Se$_2$. At 4.2 K, an in-plane magnetic field up to 25 T activates a dark-exciton line 14.2$\pm$1.3 meV below the bright exciton while suppressing the bright-exciton emission by about 85\%. A bright-dark mixing model quantitatively captures the coupled energy and intensity evolution with an effective in-plane $g$ factor of $|g_{\parallel}|=5.2\pm0.2$. Alloying is crucial to the effect, as it brings the system close to the bright-dark crossover, where a small bright-dark splitting is combined with unusually strong in-plane magnetic coupling. This places the system in a regime where field-induced level repulsion raises the bright-like branch and strongly depletes its thermal population. These results identify a general route to magnetic control of exciton populations through engineering of the bright-dark hierarchy.

item.title: [7] Rashba-controlled emergence and reversal of critical-field anisotropy in p-wave magnet--superconductor hybrids
item.description:
Last authors: Dong-Hui Xu, Chui-Zhen Chen

Authors: Rui-Xiang Cheng, Zhao Gong, Dong-Hui Xu, Chui-Zhen Chen

Score 7/10 B_IMPORTANT_CONDMAT

Why: Relevant theoretical study on superconductor heterostructures with magnetic coupling.

Tags: #superconduct #heterostructure #theory

Abstract: We show that tuning Rashba spin-orbit coupling can change the in-plane field direction along which an $s$-wave superconductor is most susceptible to Zeeman depairing. We consider a two-dimensional $s$-wave superconductor subject to an odd-parity exchange field induced by a $p$-wave magnet. Without Rashba coupling, the out-of-plane exchange field enhances the in-plane critical field but leaves its angular response exactly isotropic, despite the anisotropic magnetic spin texture. Minimizing the Bogoliubov--de Gennes grand potential over uniform singlet pairing, we find that increasing Rashba coupling first generates and then reverses the principal-axis critical-field contrast, switching the minimum-critical-field direction by $90^{\circ}$. Equal principal-axis fields at the intervening compensation point coexist with residual angular modulation. We interpret the reversal through competing momentum-dependent depairing contributions from the magnetic and Rashba spin textures, while the on-site singlet pairing channel remains unchanged. Direction-dependent discontinuous collapses of the order parameter further shape the critical-field curves. These results identify a tunable directional paramagnetic response within the uniform-pairing sector. In heterostructures with sufficient electrostatic tunability of interfacial Rashba coupling, this reversal would enable gate control of the easy-depairing axis without reorienting the magnetic texture.

item.title: [8] Magnetic-Field Effects on the Electronic States of the K4 Lattice
item.description:
Last authors: Shouya Yoshida, Katsunori Wakabayashi

Authors: Katsuhiro Takahashi, Shouya Yoshida, Katsunori Wakabayashi

Score 8/10 B_IMPORTANT_CONDMAT

Why: Electronic structure study of K4 lattice with magnetic field, relevant to topological materials.

Tags: #material #Dirac #electronicstructure

Abstract: We investigate the electronic states of the K$_4$ lattice in a uniform magnetic field within a nearest-neighbor tight-binding model. The K$_4$ lattice is a \rev{noncentrosymmetric three-dimensional network with triple-Dirac cones at the $\Gamma$ and H points}. By fixing the Bloch momentum component parallel to the field, the Peierls-substituted tight-binding problem reduces to an effective two-dimensional problem and yields a Hofstadter spectrum \rev{whose self-similar subpatterns reflect the geometry of the lattice projected onto the plane perpendicular to the field}. A square-like substructure emerges on the flux scale $\phi = 1/8$ for $\bm{B}\parallel[100]$, and honeycomb- and triangular-like substructures emerge on the finer scale $\phi = 1/32$ for $\bm{B}\parallel[111]$\rev{. Here $\phi$ is the flux through the elementary plaquette of the projected lattice, and these scales correspond to one flux quantum per projected unit cell. Owing to the screw axes of the chiral K$_4$ network, the field-parallel momentum acts as an additional flux, which, for commensurate values of this momentum, shifts the spectrum along the flux axis and brings the second triple-Dirac cone at the H point into the magnetic spectrum}. In the weak-field limit, we derive the Landau-level structure from a low-energy effective Hamiltonian around the $\Gamma$ point. The three-component nature of the triple-Dirac cone gives rise to a cubic secular equation, whose solutions describe how a pseudospin-flat branch coexists with two relativistic Landau ladders \rev{and a single chiral $n=0$ level dispersing linearly along the field, in agreement with the lattice calculation}.

item.title: [9] Persistent Photo-Enhancement of Molecular Orbital Excitations in the Kondo Insulator FeSb2
item.description:
Last authors: Dung-Hai Lee, Robert J. Birgeneau

Authors: Ke-Jun Xu, Nathan Giles-Donovan, Paulina Majchrzak, et al.

Score 9/10 A_MUST_READ

Why: author whitelist: Zhi-Xun Shen

Tags: #Kondo #phonon

Abstract: When insulators are excited by photons with above-gap energies, photo-doped carriers are transiently generated. Typically, orbital excitations weaken and broaden due to increased screening by these transient carriers, followed by a few-ps recovery via phonon thermalization. Here we report the observation of anomalous dynamics of many-body molecular orbital excitations in the narrow-gap Kondo insulator FeSb$_2$. In the pumped X-ray absorption spectra following excitation with 1~$\mu$m photons, we observe a transient transfer of absorption intensity from the delocalized states at the main absorption peak to the localized molecular orbital states at the pre-edge. At the resonance of the low-energy molecular orbital excitations, the pumped resonant inelastic X-ray spectra show an approximately 30\% intensity increase at a pump fluence of 11 mJ/cm$^2$ concomitant with the emergence of an energy gain feature. While the energy gain feature disappears after about 1-2~ps, the increased molecular orbital excitation intensities partially persist for at least 50~ps with no discernible energy shift. These observations require the invocation of a many-body excitation picture beyond single particle population changes.

item.description:
Last authors: Shingo Kobayashi, Yasuhiro Asano

Authors: Tomoya Sano, Satoshi Ikegaya, Shingo Kobayashi, Yasuhiro Asano

Abstract: We propose a model that explains the mechanism of pressure-induced superconductivity in a bilayer metal. item.description:
Last authors: V. M. Kovalev, I. G. Savenko

Score 7/10 B_IMPORTANT_CONDMAT

Why: Experimental relevance to superconducting heterostructure probes.

Abstract: The surface photogalvanic effect is a powerful tool for generating macroscopic direct currents in centrosymmetric film structures via asymmetric scattering of carriers at film boundaries. Here, we uncover a fundamentally distinct regime of photoinduced transport in normal metal-superconductor heterostructures, in which the macroscopic photocurrent is governed by Andreev scattering at the interface rather than by classical scattering. We demonstrate that the interplay between asymmetric surface scattering and Andreev retroreflection yields a giant, strongly frequency-dependent anomalous photocurrent. Strikingly, the electron-hole conversion at the normal-superconducting interface dictates a macroscopic sign reversal of the photogalvanic current across the superconducting transition, and induces non-analytic spectral kinks exactly at the pairing gap frequency. item.description:
Last authors: Harold Y. Hwang, Yijun Yu

Authors: Yidi Liu, Yaoju Tarn, Lopa Bhatt, et al.

Why: Experimental study on nickelate thin films, directly relevant to electronic materials interest.

Abstract: Ambient-pressure superconductivity above 40 K has been realized in bilayer nickelate thin films on SrLaAlO$_4$ (001), yet resistive measurements often exhibit incomplete zero-resistance states and/or two-step superconducting transitions of unresolved origin. item.title: [7] Spin fluctuations and nearly isotropic quasiparticles in the doped three-dimensional Hubbard model
item.description:
Last authors: Kun Chen, Youjin Deng

Authors: Pengcheng Hou, Kun Chen, Youjin Deng

Score 7/10 B_IMPORTANT_CONDMAT

Why: Benchmark study on Hubbard model spin fluctuations, relevant to strongly correlated systems.

Tags: #theory #Hubbard #electronicstructure

Abstract: Away from half filling and above its Neel temperature, the three-dimensional Hubbard model is a paramagnetic metal with antiferromagnetic spin fluctuations, where controlled momentum-resolved results have been lacking. Using connected-determinant diagrammatic Monte Carlo, we compute the momentum-resolved self-energy for n = 0.4-0.95, T/t = 0.05-0.33 and U/t = 4-8, and the full-zone spin susceptibility at twelve of these points, focusing on U/t = 4. At U/t = 4 and toward half filling the spin fluctuations become strong: for n = 0.7-0.9 at T/t = 0.14 they enhance the susceptibility peak up to sevenfold and raise the momentum-dependent part of the scattering rate to four to five times its second-order value. They are driven by an effective spin interaction screened to about 2U/3 and nearly uniform over the zone. Yet the peak height is set by the slightly smaller value of this interaction at the peak wave vector, and near magnetic order this small difference changes the height by a large factor. Two-particle self-consistent theory reproduces the peak because its sum rule fixes its single constant interaction near this value, but for n = 0.7-0.9 at T/t = 0.14 its self-energy overestimates the local scattering rate and underestimates the momentum-dependent part. Though strong, the fluctuations are short ranged, with a correlation length of at most about two lattice spacings, and for n = 0.7-0.9 and T/t >= 0.14 the scattering rate near the Fermi surface varies by at most about 1% at fixed band energy, without hot spots. At U/t = 4 dynamical mean-field theory (DMFT) reproduces the local scattering rate and quasiparticle weight within a few percent, and the nonlocal part it misses is approximately a function of the band energy. item.description:

Why: Experimental study on Berry curvature and anomalous Hall effects in itinerant magnets.

Tags: #material #transport #anomalousHall

Abstract: SrRuO$_3$ is a canonical itinerant ferromagnet that continues to serve as a fertile platform for exploring spin-orbit coupled transport and topological responses in correlated oxide metals. Here, we investigate a (110)-oriented epitaxial SrRuO3 thin film on DyScO$_3$, where crystallographic anisotropy allows for symmetry-resolved charge transport along orthogonal in-plane directions. We uncover two principal findings. First, the resistance above the Curie temperature $T_{c,on}\approx 165$ K exhibits strong anisotropy, consistent with directionally dependent spin-fluctuation scattering. Below $T_{c,on}$, this anisotropy nearly vanishes, despite persistent structural inequivalence, due to isotropic electron-magnon and electron-electron scattering processes. Second, the application of a magnetic field reveals a striking directional contrast in the linear magnetoresistance (MR): it remains negative and saturates along [001], but changes sign and becomes positive along $[1\bar{1}0]$ below $T_0=145$ K. In contrast, the quadratic MR term is identical for both directions and peaks near $T_{\mathrm{OHE}}^*=155$ K, where the ordinary Hall coefficient crosses zero, consistent with carrier compensation under a two-band scenario. A sign change in the anomalous Hall signal at $T_{\mathrm{AHE}}^*=150$ K is consistent with a temperature-dependent redistribution of Berry-curvature contributions near the Fermi level. item.description:
Last authors: Hua Jiang, X. C. Xie

Authors: Zhi-Qiang Zhang, Shuguang Cheng, Hongfang Liu, Hailong Li, Hua Jiang, X. C. Xie

Why: Topological transport in 3D systems relevant to Weyl/Dirac research.

Abstract: Understanding the three-dimensional (3D) quantum Hall effect, characterized by a Chern vector rather than a single Chern number, has been a central pursuit in topological physics. Crucially, this collective response manifests as a quantized Hall conductance $G_{xy}=\pm(mL_y+nL_z)e^2/h$, with a distinctive dependence on both Chern-vector components and sample dimensions. item.description:
Last authors: Thierry Giamarchi, X\^i-Wen Guan

Authors: Hai-Ying Cui, Yi-Cong Yu, Aashish Kafle, et al.

Score 7/10 B_IMPORTANT_CONDMAT

Why: Relevant study on 1D liquids, quasi-1D materials, and spin-charge separation.

Tags: #quasi-1D #theory #Luttinger

Abstract: One-dimensional (1D) interacting Fermi gases underpin a rich variety of quantum liquids, ranging from the Tomonaga-Luttinger liquid and the Fulde-Ferrell-Larkin-Ovchinnikov paired state to the Luther-Emery liquid (LEL). Notably, the LEL-characterized by gapless excitations in charge or spin degree of freedom and gapped excitations in the other-has long been theoretically predicted but has eluded definitive experimental observation to date. By exactly solving the attractive Yang-Gaudin model via the Bethe ansatz, we fully determine the low-energy excitation spectra for both spin and charge channels. For fully paired fermions, the spectrum features gapped spin excitation coexisting with gapless charge excitation. We further employ bosonization to derive analytical expressions for the dynamical structure factor (DSF) of the gapped spin excitation, which is a long-standing challenge in this study. In the trapped gas, we find that the spin Bragg spectroscopy peak occurs at a much higher frequency than the charge-mode peak, where the splitting frequency between these two peaks scales approximately linearly with the interaction strength. Crucially, the spin gap manifests as a sharp threshold in the spin DSF, below which spectral weight is completely absent, proving a direct and unambiguous spectroscopic fingerprint of the LEL. Our work establishes quasi-1D trapped attractive Fermi gases as a pristine experimental platform for the long-sought direct observation of the LEL.

Abstract: Nonreciprocal charge transport provides an effective approach for probing direction dependent charge dynamics and spin-momentum-locked electronic states. Here, we report highly gate-tunable nonreciprocal charge transport in dual-gated BiSbTeSe2 topological insulator device. The second-harmonic longitudinal resistance is linear in both current and magnetic field. item.description:
Last authors: Yuxuan Mu, Xiangang Wan

Authors: Xinhai Tu, Di Wang, Yuxuan Mu, Xiangang Wan

Why: Theoretical framework for magnons in altermagnets, relevant to magnetic topological materials and transport.

Tags: #theory #magnons #altermagnetism #spin-orbitcoupling #transport

Abstract: Spin groups provide the natural symmetry framework for the isotropic Heisenberg model, in which spin and lattice degrees of freedom are separable. They have recently found broad applications in describing electronic band structure, magnon band topology, and transport phenomena. However, a typical spin Hamiltonian describing magnons contains not only isotropic Heisenberg exchange but also anisotropic interactions induced by spin-orbit coupling (SOC), including the Dzyaloshinskii-Moriya (DM) interaction, the Gamma exchange, and the single-ion anisotropy (SIA), which strongly influence magnon properties. More recently, some studies have also revealed relativistic magnon transport phenomena in altermagnets. Such systems typically exhibit partial spin-lattice locking, but are commonly assumed to be described by conventional magnetic groups. Here, we develop a systematic symmetry framework, generalized spin groups, for magnons. We first classify the symmetries of Heisenberg, DM, Gamma, and SIA interactions. The resulting classification contains 6 spin-only groups, together with a total of 161 nontrivial spin groups. The symmetries of magnetically ordered phases are then obtained through spontaneous symmetry breaking of the corresponding parent groups for spin Hamiltonians. We also identify 6 spin-only groups for ordered states, which generate 90, 264, 157, 264, 387, and 598 nontrivial spin groups, respectively. Finally, we apply generalized spin groups to the magnon thermal conductivity and spin conductivity tensors and derive all the symmetry-allowed forms. Our results provide a unified symmetry framework for analyzing magnon transport both with and without SOC, yielding more refined constraints on magnon responses.

item.title: [7] Time-Reversal Symmetry in Artificial Topological Graphene Rings
item.description:
Last authors: J. A. da Silva Neto, G. Q. Garcia, A. M. de M. Carvalho, C. Furtado

Score 7/10 B_IMPORTANT_CONDMAT

Why: Theoretical study of time-reversal symmetry and electronic properties in topological graphene rings.

Tags: #theory #graphene #Diracfermions #topological #time-reversalsymmetry

Abstract: We study an artificial graphene ring described by the low-energy two-valley Dirac Hamiltonian with a uniform mass term. When the ring is threaded by an Aharonov-Bohm flux, the problem reduces to a second-order radial equation solved by Bessel functions. We give the exact secular equation and, for narrow rings, closed expressions for the spectrum and the persistent current. We then add a uniform magnetic field perpendicular to the plane. The radial problem is solved with confluent hypergeometric functions, and the persistent current and magnetization are written as derivatives of a secular determinant from which the spurious roots have been removed. Besides the usual orbital coupling, the field enters through a valley-dependent term that comes from the Dirac structure and lifts the valley degeneracy. A weak-field expansion, accurate up to corrections of order B^4, gives this valley splitting explicitly and separates the diamagnetic and paramagnetic contributions to the susceptibility. Finally, we work out what time reversal implies for the spectrum. Physical time reversal, which exchanges the valleys, leads to an exact relation between levels at opposite fields. The effective single-valley time reversal, on the other hand, is broken by the mass term and by the boundary conditions, yet leaves no trace in the zero-field spectrum. Numerical results for the spectrum, the persistent current, and the magnetization illustrate the analysis.

item.title: [9] Adiabatic confinement and number-theoretic spectra of massless Dirac fermions in twisted trilayer graphene
item.description:
Last authors: Changwon Park, Young-Woo Son

Authors: Kunihiro Yananose, Changwon Park, Young-Woo Son

Why: Theory on novel confinement of massless Dirac fermions in twisted trilayer graphene, very relevant.; demoted from A: broad CM, not direct user/project hit

Tags: #theory #graphene #twistedbilayer #Diracfermions #electronicstructure

Abstract: Electrons in graphene move like massless relativistic particles, making them exceptionally mobile but difficult to trap because Klein tunnelling permits unimpeded passage through electrostatic barriers. This challenge extends to atomic collapse and hadron confinement. Twisted trilayers form Bernal and rhombohedral domains joined by smooth boundaries, bringing their carriers into contact. Here we show that a new mechanism, distinct from established approaches, confines massless fermions in equilateral triangular Bernal domains without mass barriers, bulk gaps or physical edges. Simulations and analytical modeling reveal that massless carriers have no adiabatic continuation into rhombohedral domains, while escape through nonadiabatic coupling to massive carriers is exponentially suppressed by smooth stacking variation. Perfect reflection in the adiabatic limit turns Bernal domains into quantum cavities in a gapless, edgeless metal. Striking density-of-states oscillations encode Eisenstein-integer arithmetic, linking energies and degeneracies to norms and prime factorizations. These findings bring relativistic confinement and number theory into experimentally accessible electronic spectra.

item.title: [7] Density Saturation and Autocorrelation Characteristics of Interlayer Exciton Ensembles in MoSe2/WSe2 Heterostructures
item.description:
Last authors: Ursula Wurstbauer, Alexander W. Holleitner

Authors: Mirco Troue, Johannes Figueiredo, Alina Scheuermann, et al.

Score 7/10 B_IMPORTANT_CONDMAT

Why: Experimental study of interlayer excitons and Mott physics in van der Waals heterostructures.

Abstract: We investigate interlayer excitons in MoSe$_2$/WSe$_2$ heterostructures using time-resolved photoluminescence and second-order autocorrelation measurements across a wide range of excitation powers and bath temperatures. By analyzing the photoluminescence amplitude and lifetime of the interlayer exciton state with the lowest emission energy, we extract a corresponding density-temperature diagram. The extracted exciton density exhibits a saturation at approximately $10^{13}$cm$^{-2}$, consistent with values predicted for a Mott transition of interlayer exciton ensembles in van der Waals heterostructures. Abstract: $\mathrm{NiPS_3}$ has attracted considerable attention, yet the origin of its intriguing magnetic behaviors remains elusive due to limited insight into its low-energy anisotropy. Here, high-field torque magnetometry measurements are performed, revealing a previously unrecognized anisotropic spin response that reflects interaction terms beyond the standard XY or XXZ models. In combination with relativistic density functional theory calculations and magnetic force response theory, an effective low-energy spin Hamiltonian is constructed, elucidating not only the observed anomalous magnetic behavior but also other recent experiments. The generalized Hamiltonian can serve as the important fundamental ground for future study, and our approach adopted here will hopefully be relevant to many other related material systems.

item.title: [8] Saturating T2 resistivity in iron-based superconductors
item.description:
Last authors: M. Lourdes Amig\'o, Jorge I. Facio

Score 8/10 B_IMPORTANT_CONDMAT

Why: Transport and correlations in iron-based superconductors, including nematicity, highly relevant.

Tags: #unconventionalsuperconductivity #iron-basedsuperconductors #nematicity #transport #stronglycorrelatedelectronsystems

Abstract: Many correlated metals exhibit a crossover from low-temperature $\rho \propto T^{2}$ behavior to a slower increase of the resistivity at elevated temperatures. Distinguishing phonon scattering from electron--electron correlations as the origin of this crossover is experimentally challenging. We introduce a simple phenomenological framework that isolates the contribution responsible for the high-temperature saturating tendency. This approach reveals a clear contrast between systems well known for the predominance of electron--phonon scattering and several iron-based superconductors. For the latter, the conductivity can be expressed as the sum of a Fermi-liquid-like term ($\propto 1/T^{2}$) and a temperature-independent component, which together describe $\rho(T)$ up to $\sim 250$ K in LiFeAs, KFe$_2$As$_2$, and KCaFe$_4$As$_4$. In FeSe, the same approach identifies a similar regime above the nematic transition, with a pronounced change toward nearly linear-in-$T$ resistivity below it. We discuss these findings in the broader context of coherence and electronic correlations in Hund's metals.

item.description:
Last authors: S. A. Grigera, R. A. Borzi

Authors: T. Vignau Costa, J. Colbois, G. L. Rossini, et al.

Abstract: We investigate a nearest-neighbor Ising model on the kagome lattice coupled to elastic lattice distortions. By integrating out the lattice degrees of freedom, we derive an approximate spin-only description in terms of a kagome \(J_1\)-\(J_2\)-\(J_{3}\) Ising model with interactions extending to third nearest-neighbors. Using tensor network methods complemented by classical Monte Carlo simulations, we revisit its zero-temperature phase diagram and characterize the ground states studied more than thirty years ago. Their quasi long-range order is reflected in Bragg-like peaks in the structure factors; we relate this, and other properties, to diverse phases found in Ising and Heisenberg models. Finally, we trace the trajectories generated by the magnetoelastic coupling through the effective-model phase diagram, explaining the emergence of self-frustration for the unfrustrated magnetoelastic model with ferromagnetic interactions.

item.description:
Last authors: Mikhail D. Lukin, Philip Kim

Authors: Andr\'es M. Mier Valdivia, Pavel E. Dolgirev, Grace H. Chen, et al.

Score 7/10 B_IMPORTANT_CONDMAT

Why: Experimental study of correlated excitonic phenomena in 2D van der Waals materials.

Tags: #excitons #vanderWaals #correlated

Abstract: When an ensemble of emitters is confined within an optical wavelength, its radiation can become correlated, leading to cooperative emission. In two-dimensional (2D) transition metal dichalcogenide (TMD) electron-hole bilayers, strong light-matter coupling enables the formation of interlayer excitons (IXs), long-lived dipolar excitations that provide an ideal setting for emergent collective phenomena. Here, we engineer an atomically thin light-emitting diode (LED) that generates electroluminescence (EL) from electrically injected IXs that are confined near the sample edges by an edge-enhanced fringing electric field. By measuring Hanbury-Brown-Twiss photon-photon correlations, we find pronounced signatures of collective decay in the form of large photon bunching followed by finite delay antibunching and bunching revivals. These emitter correlation signatures disappear when free charge carriers are doped to form a degenerate Fermi sea but are enhanced by the introduction of localized electrons. The results are consistent with a many-body quantum master equation that models the steady-state superradiant photon statistics of incoherently injected IXs. Our work establishes steady-state cooperative emission in a 2D TMD LED as a platform for studying strong light-matter interactions in electrically driven, non-equilibrium phases of Bose-Fermi mixtures.

item.description:
Last authors: Michael A. Sentef, Sang Soon Oh

Authors: Kyle S. Netherwood, Juan I. Aranzadi, Nils Jacobsen, Michael A. Sentef, Sang Soon Oh

Score 8/10 B_IMPORTANT_CONDMAT

Why: Theoretical framework for light-driven Weyl semimetals, relevant to ARPES/optical spectroscopy.

Tags: #Weyl #Floquet #photocurrent

Abstract: Structured light provides a route to controlling quantum materials not only through its polarization, but also through its spatial profile and orbital angular momentum (OAM). We develop real space theories of a Weyl semimetal driven by a vortex beam and show that optical OAM generates highly localized Floquet vortex states with pronounced circulating photocurrents. Exploiting cylindrical symmetry, we derive a Bogoliubov-de Gennes-like radial equation that resolves the states by angular momentum and reveals their evolution between the light-dressed Weyl cones. For Laguerre-Gaussian beams, the spatially varying drive produces strong hybridization between localized vortex states and bulk states. We complement this continuum description with a Wilson-lattice formulation that retains the full two-dimensional spatial structure and enables direct calculation of local photocurrents. Both approaches consistently identify OAM-induced vortex states localized around the beam axis. The lattice calculation further shows that these states support substantially stronger circulating current densities than the more extended surface states, with the largest current densities associated with the most strongly localized, low-angular-momentum vortex modes. Our results establish optical OAM as a tunable control parameter for creating and manipulating localized current-carrying states in Weyl systems and provide a real-space framework for studying photocurrents generated by spatially structured light.

Abstract: We evaluate the electron scattering properties in CoSi thin films having either twin (heterochiral) or non-twin (homochiral) grain boundaries using first-principles quantum transport calculations. We find that scattering across a twin grain boundary is more resistive than scattering across a non-twin grain boundary and that non-twin grain boundaries have a greater percentage of surface conduction than twin grain boundaries. This is corroborated by the transmission eigenstate profiles, which show that the surface Fermi-arc electrons can transmit past the non-twin grain boundaries between homochiral domains on the same surface without significant backscattering. In contrast, these surface electrons get scattered along the twin grain boundaries between heterochiral domains to the opposite surface, resulting in partial forward transmission and partial backscattering that yields higher grain-boundary resistivity. This work helps elucidate the complexities of electron transport in chiral topological semimetals for potential application in next-generation nano-interconnects.

item.description:
Last authors: Jyotirmoy Sau

Why: Nonlinear Hall response studies are highly relevant to Berry curvature and topological materials.

Abstract: A Berry-curvature dipole can produce a nonlinear Hall current even when the linear Hall response vanishes, but symmetry alone does not determine its magnitude or magnetic tunability. item.title: [7] Acceleration of CTQMC via Denoising Diffusion Models with Auxiliary Spectral Functions
item.description:
Last authors: Rishi Rao, Li Zhu

Score 7/10 B_IMPORTANT_CONDMAT

Why: Significant methodological advancement for solving correlated systems (DMFT) in materials.

Tags: #DMFT #correlated #method

Abstract: Continuous-time Quantum Monte Carlo (CTQMC) impurity solvers are a numerically exact, but expensive, option for solving the Dynamical Mean Field Theory (DMFT) equations, with statistical noise from undersampling presenting a major challenge to low temperature studies. This noise is especially egregious within the sampled self-energy, which can destabilize the self-consistency loop upon insertion into the Dyson equation. In this work, we introduce a neural denoiser for fermionic imaginary time Green's functions based on the diffusion model architecture trained on synthetic data. The network predicts positive and normalized auxiliary spectral functions consistent with the noisy imaginary axis CTQMC data, which is then refined via autodifferentiation to match the measured self-energy, its first two high-frequency moments, and impurity occupation similar to the Constrained Residual Minimization (CRM) method. This leads to Green's functions and self-energies that are causal by design. Through this denoising framework we are able to reduce the required CTQMC measurement steps by a factor of 10-100. We benchmark our method with a half-filled Hubbard model on a Bethe lattice, a two-patch Dynamical Cluster Approximation (DCA) of the two-dimensional Hubbard model, and the SrVO$_3$ system. We reproduce the Mott transition upon increasing Coulomb interaction for the half-filled Hubbard model with only 5000 CTQMC measurements, the pseudogap transition for the DCA two-dimensional Hubbard model with only 5$\times$10$^5$ measurements, and match the spectral function of SrVO$_3$ with 50 times fewer measurements than the reference. Since we generate auxiliary spectral functions, we recover the approximate spectral functions of the systems for free without performing analytic continuation.

item.title: [7] Parallel Omnidirectional Atom Rearrangement with Dynamic Holograms
item.description:
Last authors: Kang-Kuen Ni, Norman Y. Yao

Authors: Samuel A. Engel, Dewei Gong, Ziguang Lin, Lysander Christakis, Kang-Kuen Ni, Norman Y. Yao

Score 7/10 B_IMPORTANT_CONDMAT

Why: Large-scale kagome lattice assembly using optical tweezers is highly relevant to kagome metal research.

Tags: #kagome #coldatoms #lattice

Abstract: The ability to assemble and reconfigure individual atoms is central to performing quantum science using optical tweezer arrays. Here, we demonstrate parallel omnidirectional atom transport and rearrangement using dynamic holograms generated by a single kilohertz-rate spatial light modulator. By carefully characterizing survival and heating, we show that atoms remain confined even when successive holograms are commanded before the liquid crystal has settled, enabling significantly faster transport. To generate holograms in real time, we develop and implement a warm-start, weighted Gerchberg-Saxton algorithm that achieves performance comparable to neural-network methods without requiring any training. Combining these techniques, we assemble ytterbium atoms into a 2078-site kagome lattice with 99.0% mean filling. In addition, we demonstrate parallel transport between array layers, combining axial and transverse motion to reconfigure atoms in three dimensions. Our approach is readily adaptable to existing tweezer platforms and provides a method for large-scale SLM-based atom assembly as well as programmable three-dimensional control.

item.title: [7] Direct Urca process facilitated by non-Fermi-liquid quantum criticality
item.description:
Last authors: Hao-Fu Zhu, Guo-Zhu Liu

Score 7/10 B_IMPORTANT_CONDMAT

Why: Connects non-Fermi liquid and quantum criticality to fundamental physical processes.

Tags: #quantumcriticality #non-Fermiliquid #superconductivity

Abstract: Conventional Fermi-liquid theories of dense nuclear matter predict that the direct Urca process requires a proton fraction above a threshold of $Y_p \approx 0.11$--$0.15$, which is rarely reached in low-mass neutron stars. Here we show that this stringent kinematic constraint is drastically relaxed by the non-Fermi liquid behavior arising from superfluid and superconducting quantum criticality in neutron stars. In the non-Fermi-liquid regimes, nucleons have a smooth momentum occupation without a sharp Fermi surface, and their chemical potentials develop a logarithmic temperature dependence. These intrinsic features fundamentally alter the standard $\beta$-equilibrium relation. Consequently, direct Urca neutrino emission can be activated even at low nuclear densities. This modifies the long-standing Urca-threshold paradigm and indicates that direct Urca process has the opportunity to occur in low-mass neutron stars.

item.description:
Last authors: Thomas Eckl, Michael J. Hartmann

Why: Applies DMFT to high-Tc cuprate materials; highly relevant for correlated electron electronic structure.

Abstract: We design a hybrid quantum-classical computational workflow, combining density functional theory and dynamical mean-field theory, to investigate the electronic properties of CaCuO2, a parent structure of high-temperature cuprate superconductors. Our approach uses a quantum algorithm as an impurity solver that is based on variational quantum compressed time evolution to compute the time-dependent Greens function on an IBM Heron quantum device. Utilizing error mitigation techniques and a Lehmann representation fitting procedure, we extract the density of states from the signal in the accessible time regime. However, we find that the required numerical accuracy for full DMFT self-consistency exceeds current hardware capabilities, indicating that practical real-material DMFT applications will necessitate post-NISQ hardware developments.

item.title: [7] Floquet ground state order
item.description:
Last authors: Paul M. Schindler, Marin Bukov

Authors: Suman Mondal, Paul M. Schindler, Marin Bukov

Score 7/10 B_IMPORTANT_CONDMAT

Why: Studies Floquet-driven correlated phases and time crystals, of interest for modern non-equilibrium experiments.

Tags: #Floquet #correlated #many-body

Abstract: Clean, interacting, periodically driven systems are believed to thermalize to featureless, infinite-temperature states that preclude the formation of stable ordered states. Here, we show stable quantum order, distinct from prethermal order, and its phase transitions in the ground state of the average-energy operator. Decomposing the time evolution into geometric and average-energy dynamics, we apply Geometric Floquet theory to identify the Floquet ground state. We derive a general variational principle to compute the Floquet ground state in large interacting periodically driven systems, and use it to develop a matrix product state algorithm. In driven nonintegrable chains of more than 100 interacting spins, our numerical simulations exhibit a gapped, area-law entangled Floquet ground state in extended parameter regimes; the ground-state manifold can support both dressed equilibrium order (e.g., Floquet antiferromagnets) and inherently nonequilibrium order (e.g., ground-state time crystals). This quantum order is protected by a finite average-energy gap, which closes at phase transition points upon changing model parameters. We decompose Floquet phases of matter into their equilibrium and nonequilibrium elements: whereas the Floquet ground state at any fixed time is a representative of an equilibrium phase of matter, the nonequilibrium content is entirely produced by the drive holonomy and is geometric. Finally, we identify quasilocal counterdiabatic driving as a mechanism for the stability against heating of gapped Floquet ground states in nonintegrable quantum systems, and argue why Floquet ground states evade the Eigenstate Thermalization Hypothesis. Our work enables the study of interacting nonequilibrium matter deep into the many-body regime, and lays the foundations for the engineering of strongly correlated ordered quantum states.

item.description:
Last authors: Felipe P\'erez Riffo, Eric Su\'arez Morell

Authors: Kevin J. U. Vidarte, Caio Lewenkopf, F. Crasto de Lima, R. Hiroki Miwa, Felipe P\'erez Riffo, Eric Su\'arez Morell

Why: Directly explains STM/conductivity measurements in twisted graphene using electronic structure.

Tags: #STM #STS #graphene #twistedbilayer #bandstructure

Abstract: This study theoretically investigates the contact conductance in twisted bilayer graphene (TBG), addressing recent experimental observations from scanning tunneling microscopy (STM) and conductive atomic force microscopy (c-AFM). These experiments revealed a surprising non-monotonic current pattern as a function of the TBG rotation angle $\theta$, with a peak at $\theta \approx 5^\circ$, a finding that markedly departs from the well-known magic angle TBG behavior. To elucidate this phenomenon, we develop a theoretical and computational framework {based on the system's local density of states, and evaluate the contact current over the energy range of states that contribute to the junction}. {Our results, obtained for both relaxed and rigid TBG structures, indicate that the conductance maximum at $\theta \approx 5^{\circ}$ is not primarily caused by structural relaxation or by changes in the AA-stacking area: the maximum persists, at essentially the same angle, in rigid (unreconstructed) lattices.} Instead, we attribute this peak to the evolution of the electronic band structure, specifically the shifting of van Hove singularities (vHs) toward the Fermi level as the twist angle decreases. The precise location of the maximum tracks the energy window of states participating in the contact, which in contact-mode measurements is set by the local doping under the metallic tip rather than by the small applied bias alone. We show that the angle of maximum conductance shifts with carrier doping, a dependence that is directly testable by electrostatic gating and that a purely structural mechanism cannot produce.

item.title: [8] Quantum Spin Singlet Ground State with Large Excitation Gap in the S = 3/2 quasi-1D van der Waals materials MoX3 (X = I, Br)
item.description:
Last authors: Alexander A. Balandin, Roger K. Lake

Authors: Jordan Teeter, Topojit Debnath, Harshil Goyal, et al.

Score 8/10 B_IMPORTANT_CONDMAT

Why: Experimental study of spin-singlet ground state and triplons in quasi-1D vdW materials via neutron scattering.

Tags: #quasi-1D #van_der_Waals #neutron_scattering #magnetism #experiment #DFT

Abstract: We report the first experimental evidence for a quantum-disordered spin-singlet ground state and gapped triplon excitations in quasi-one-dimensional van der Waals materials. The insulating van der Waals trihalides MoI3 and MoBr3 are analyzed in a combined thermodynamic, spectroscopic, and theoretical investigation. These materials contain structurally dimerized atomic chains of face-sharing octahedra with alternating short and long Mo-Mo separations along the chain direction. Temperature-dependent bulk magnetic susceptibility measurements reveal a broad thermally activated response consistent with a large spin gap. Inelastic neutron scattering (INS) spectra provide direct evidence of a collective spin gap at an exceptionally large energy transfer of ~ 30 meV (~ 348 K) for MoBr3. The absence of low-energy magnetic spectral weight and the activated susceptibility are inconsistent with a conventional classical antiferromagnetic ground state. Instead, they point to a spin-singlet ground state with a large singlet-triplet excitation gap. To identify the microscopic origin of this gap, we perform density matrix renormalization group (DMRG) calculations on one-dimensional spin chains using exchange constants derived from density functional theory (DFT). The dominance of the single dimer exchange term allows the inter-dimer coupling along the chain and between chains to be treated using perturbation theory. Intrachain exchange lowers the isolated-dimer triplet energy by producing a dispersive triplon band. INS data show the triplon bandwidth to be ~ 20 meV. Interchain coupling produces negligible additional bandwidth on the order of 1 meV. The INS measurements directly establish quantum spin-singlet and triplon physics in MoBr3 with a large singlet-triplet gap on the scale of room temperature, while the susceptibility and theoretical results indicate closely analogous behavior in MoI3.

item.title: [7] Topological Charge-2ne Superconductivity and Clustering Hierarchy
item.description:
Last authors: Hui Yang, Congjun Wu

Authors: Zhi-Qiang Gao, Yan-Qi Wang, Hui Yang, Congjun Wu

Why: Theoretical framework for topological charge-2ne superconductivity with non-Abelian anyons.

Tags: #topological_superconductivity #theory #strongly_correlated

Abstract: Charge-$2ne$ superconductors condense clusters of more than two electrons, extending superconductivity beyond Cooper pairing. They exhibit distinctive signatures including fractional flux quantization $h/(2ne)$ and are actively being explored in strongly correlated systems. We develop a general framework for constructing and characterizing \emph{topological} charge-$2ne$ superconductors by combining wavefunction and field theory approaches. These reveal that higher-charge superconductivity supports a richer hierarchy of topological phases beyond the Read-Green weak-strong pairing dichotomy, with distinct internal clustering structures giving rise to different topological structures at fixed condensate charge.

item.description:
Last authors: Thierry Giamarchi, Xi-Wen Guan

Authors: Hai-Ying Cui, Yu-Hao Yeh, Randall G. Hulet, Han Pu, Thierry Giamarchi, Xi-Wen Guan

Published as: Phys. Rev. A

Why: title strong match: Luttinger liquid

Tags: #spin-chargeseparation #Luttinger

Abstract: The one-dimensional (1D) Yang-Gaudin model--an integrable $\delta$-function interacting Fermi gas, serves as a paradigm in quantum many-body physics, encompassing phenomena from spin-charge separation to the Luther-Emery liquid. However, a consistent description of the Luther-Emery liquid and the Fulde-Ferrell-Larkin-Ovchinnikov (FFLO)-like pairing states in the 1D attractive Fermi gas remains elusive. In this work, we develop a universal Tomonaga-Luttinger liquid (TLL) theory to describe the FFLO state both for the case of weak and strong binding between fermions of opposite spins. We rigorously derive a low-energy effective Hamiltonian using bosonization, revealing the emergence of a two-component TLL: one exhibiting spin-charge coupling in the weak binding regime, and another featuring charge-charge separation in the strong binding regime. For the weak binding regime, we further derive renormalization-group equations for the sine-Gordon term in the spin sector and show that this term undergoes a relevant-irrelevant phase transition driven by the magnetic field. We further analyze the dynamical correlation functions of the FFLO pairing state based on the effective Hamiltonian we constructed. Finally, we discuss experiments using ultracold atoms to elucidate the Luther-Emery liquid behavior and the subtle phenomena of spin-charge coupling and charge-charge separation.

Abstract: While deep learning offers powerful capabilities for scientific research, its application is often hindered by a lack of quantitative reliability. To address this, we introduce a probabilistic denoising framework that simultaneously extracts denoised signals and element-wise predictive uncertainties from noisy data. We demonstrate this approach on three-dimensional angle-resolved photoemission spectroscopy data, showing that the model reliably recovers the spectral features of a cuprate superconductor from Poisson-distributed noise with an average count of only 0.02 electrons per voxel. Ultimately, this approach establishes uncertainty-aware deep learning not merely as a visualization tool, but as a rigorous framework for scientific data analysis.

item.description:
Last authors: Elke Scheer, Angelo Di Bernardo

Authors: Marcel Strohmeier, Andriy Smolyanyuk, Karsten Held, et al.

Tags: #superconductivity #spin-triplet #STS #experiment #noncentrosymmetric #correlated

Abstract: Although Cooper pairs in superconductors generally condense into a spin-singlet state, spin-triplet superconductivity has attracted sustained interest since it enables dissipationless spin transport and is an important requirement for manifold topological quantum technologies. Noncentrosymmetric superconductors provide a promising route to triplet pairing because their intrinsic antisymmetric spin-orbit coupling (ASOC) can mix spin-singlet and spin-triplet states. To date, the strongest evidence for such mixed-parity superconductivity has been reported in heavy-fermion systems, where strong electronic correlations obscure the role of ASOC. Whether ASOC alone can support a substantial spin-triplet component remains unresolved. Here we show that the weakly correlated noncentrosymmetric superconductor Nb$_{18}$Re$_{82}$ (Nb-Re) hosts a mixed-parity superconducting state with a substantial spin-triplet contribution. Orientation-resolved low-temperature scanning tunneling spectroscopy reveals a strongly anisotropic quasiparticle density of states. A symmetry-constrained analysis shows that the spectroscopic dataset is explained by an order parameter combining a nodal spin-singlet component with a spin-triplet contribution reaching up to half of the singlet amplitude. These findings provide a momentum-resolved determination of a mixed-parity superconducting order parameter and demonstrate that ASOC alone can foster a substantial spin-triplet component. More broadly, they establish orientation-resolved tunneling spectroscopy as a route to identifying mixed-parity superconducting states and suggest that triplet superconductivity may be more widespread among noncentrosymmetric materials than previously recognized.

Abstract: High-pressure hydrides hold the record for the highest superconducting critical temperatures across all classes of superconductors. Currently lanthanum decahydride, LaH$_{10}$, exhibits the highest critical temperature among binaries, with $T_c \approx$ 250 K at pressures between 140-180 GPa. Here, we report the synthesis of LaH$_{10\pm\delta}$ films in two DACs at pressures of 168 GPa and 176 GPa via in situ laser heating of elemental lanthanum films with ammonia borane (NH$_3$BH$_3$) as the hydrogen donor. The high-symmetry fcc lanthanum sublattice (space group $Fm\bar3m$) is resolved using synchrotron X-ray diffraction, with unit cell parameters in excellent agreement with previous studies on bulk samples. We provide confirmation of high-$T_c$ superconductivity in LaH$_{10\pm\delta}$ with highest $T_c$ of 247 K at 176 GPa evidenced in electrical measurements. The characteristic suppression of superconductivity is observed in magnetic fields. Furthermore, combined diffraction and electrical measurements reveal remarkable temporal stability of both the crystal structure and the high-$T_c$ superconductivity over the full measurement period of about 300 days post laser heating. Our work establishes film precursors using physical vapour deposition (PVD) techniques as a practical route to hydride formation, opening a pathway toward the controlled synthesis of promising ternary hydrides and the integration of micro-fabricated device geometries in diamond anvil cells.

Last authors: Zhen Ning, Rui Wang

Abstract: Universal conductance fluctuations are conventionally organized by symmetry class, but crystalline anisotropy introduces additional structure in spin transport. Here we demonstrate orientation-dependent universal spin-transport fluctuations in disordered two-dimensional $d$-wave altermagnets without spin-orbit coupling. Rotating the altermagnetic orientation changes both longitudinal spin-conductance and transverse spin-Hall conductance fluctuations, while each conserved-spin sector remains in class AI. Altermagnetic orientation controls both the fluctuation amplitudes and the development of disorder-insensitive plateaus. These plateaus become flatter and less sensitive to the altermagnetic strength over the studied parameter ranges as the orientation approaches $45^\circ$, with representative fluctuation amplitudes of approximately $0.60e/(4\pi)$ for the longitudinal spin conductance and $0.40\,e/(4\pi)$ for the spin-Hall conductance. The longitudinal fluctuation amplitude correlates strongly with anisotropy of the clean-band Fermi-velocity tensor. Spin-sector covariances explain how the conserved channels combine into total fluctuations. Our results extend anisotropy-sensitive universal-fluctuation physics to conserved-spin altermagnetic transport and establish crystalline orientation as a control parameter within a fixed symmetry class.

item.description:
Last authors: E. F. Talantsev

Why: Discusses resistivity and nematic order in iron-based superconductors, relevant to user's broader interests.

Tags: #superconductivity #ironbasedsuperconductors #nematicity #transport

Abstract: Temperature-dependent electrical resistivity $\rho(T)$ in cuprate, iron-based, and nickelate superconductors represents one of unresolved problems in modern solid-state physics, because of the high absolute value of $\rho(T)$, which, in many cases, exceeds the Ioffe-Rigel criterion, and a large difference in the $\rho(T)$ shape for samples with different doping. Here I show that the nearest neighbors parallel resistivity model (arXiv: 2607.23484) can well describe the in-plane resistivity $\rho_{ab}(T)$ in iron-based superconductors (IBS) of type 11, 111, 122, 1111, 1144 and 42214 in which the spin density wave phase or nematic order is suppressed by doping. The model is based on the postulate that $\rho_{ab}(T)$ is a sum of two parallel conduction channels, where one channel is described by the Bloch-Gr\"uneisen equation and the other by the Arrhenius hopping equation. Consequently, the variety of $\rho_{ab}(T)$ in the IBS is explained as a variation of the Debye temperature $\Theta_D$ and the hopping activation energy $E_a$. The derived Debye temperatures were used to estimate the electron-phonon coupling constant $\lambda_{e-ph}$in the studied IBS.

Abstract: The interplay between chirality and magnetism is a profound topic, spanning particle physics, condensed matter, chemistry and origin of life. In this paper, we study this interplay in the new antiferromagnet (AFM) UOTe, and we report a chiral superlattice route to spin-split topological phenomena from collinear antiferromagnetism. Pristine UOTe is a collinear AFM without Berry curvature or spin-split bands. However, we identify the spontaneous formation of a chiral superlattice in UOTe, which can be viewed as frozen chiral phonons at finite wave vector. When electrons move through the chiral superlattice, their orbital Bloch wavefunction and quantum geometry are modulated by the strong chiral superlattice potential, generating large Berry curvature in the chiral superlattice, which we detect by the nonlinear Hall effect. At 150 K, the chiral superlattice induced Berry curvature couples to the collinear AFM order, generating a giant anomalous Hall angle ~0.14 abruptly near $T_N$ that is among the largest in bulk magnets. Moreover, our spin Hanle precession measurement shows that the chiral superlattice also generates spin-polarized current from the collinear AFM, a long-standing goal in spintronics. We shed light on the supermodulation formation mechanism based on chemical ion size and physical interlayer-intralayer energy competitions, using which we propose a design principle to discover similar bond-mismatch superlattices, providing a chiral superlattice pathway through real space engineering of quantum geometry.

item.description:

Abstract: Spin triplet superconductors are of interest because of their topological properties, and their robustness to high magnetic fields. CeRh$_2$As$_2$ is a unique heavy fermion superconductor with both even-parity and candidate odd-parity superconducting phases with a special feature enabling a field induced phase transition between the two. The field induced transition which switches the parity of the Cooper pairs is enabled by a staggered antisymmetric spin orbit coupling (ASOC) interaction. The resulting Kondo lattice model leads to nearly degenerate even and odd parity superconducting states that display a field induced parity transition between an even-parity state and an odd-parity pseudospin triplet state. Abstract: Recent progress in programmable quantum simulators motivates exact benchmarks for nonequilibrium dynamics in topological quantum matter. We study the Kitaev honeycomb model driven through its critical regions by a linear ramp of the bond coupling $J_z$ over a ramp time $\tau$, comparing zigzag and armchair ribbons with fully periodic tubes. The production of excitations exhibits a geometry-dependent finite-size crossover controlled by $N_2/\sqrt{\tau}$, the ratio of the ribbon width to the Kibble--Zurek length. Periodic tubes obey the expected critical-line Kibble--Zurek scaling and serve as the boundary-free benchmark. Zigzag ribbons follow the same scaling until defect production is exponentially suppressed by a finite-width algebraic gap floor associated with the formation of Majorana edge modes, whose occupation is pinned by inversion parity. Armchair ribbons instead support transient Majorana edge modes with exponentially small gaps, producing width-parity-dependent defect plateaus: exactly one defect per unit length for odd widths and an approximate, transient plateau near one half for even widths. The quench-generated entanglement entropy and fermionic logarithmic negativity inherit the same geometry-dependent structure, and the negativity further distinguishes the coherence-borne entanglement of the Kibble--Zurek regime from the population-borne entanglement of the edge-mode plateaus. These results identify boundary Majorana modes as the mechanism controlling departures from ideal Kibble--Zurek dynamics and provide geometry-resolved benchmarks for programmable simulations of topological matter.
